DQDL rules: completeness, uniqueness, value ranges, allowed values, data types, freshness, referential integrity between datasets, custom SQLSQL (Structured Query Language)The standard language for querying and changing data in relational databases. Analytics services such as Amazon Athena and Amazon Redshift also use SQL.Glossary entryClose, and more. Dynamic rules compare with past runs (for example RowCount > avg(last(10))).
Rule recommendations: Glue analyzes a table and proposes a starting ruleset.
Anomaly detection: analyzers collect statistics over time, and ML flags unusual values or volumes that no rule describes.
Results: written to Amazon S3, sent to Amazon CloudWatch and Amazon EventBridge, so a rule on a low score can alert a team or stop a pipeline.

Volume suddenly drops, no rule for it→ leads to Anomaly detection

AWS Glue Data Quality measures and monitors the quality of data in data lakesData lakeA central store for large amounts of structured and unstructured data kept in its original form, usually in Amazon S3, which many tools can analyze. AWS Lake Formation helps build and secure one.Glossary entryClose and pipelines. You write rules in the Data Quality Definition Language (DQDL), such as "order_id is complete and unique" or "row count is greater than the average of the last 10 runs", and Glue evaluates them and gives a data quality score: the percentage of rules that pass. It is serverless, built on the open-source Deequ framework, and can also recommend rules and detect anomalies with machine learningML (Machine learning)Software that learns patterns from example data to make predictions or decisions, instead of following rules written by hand. A model is first trained on data, then used to make predictions on new data, which is called inference.Glossary entryClose.
Choose it when a question asks to check data quality automatically, stop bad data before it reaches a data lake or a training job, or watch data quality over time (MLA-C02 tasks 1.3.1 and 4.1.2).
Runs use IAM roles with access only to the tables and buckets they check; results in S3 are encrypted like other Glue outputs; Lake Formation permissions apply to governed tables.
Serverless and managed; checks in ETL jobs can stop a run so that bad data never lands, and results history supports audits.
Checks in ETL jobs scale with the job (auto scaling and Flex are supported there); incremental checks use job bookmarks or pushdown predicates so only new data is evaluated.
You pay for the compute (DPU hours) that evaluations and recommendations use, with no license. Check new partitions incrementally instead of whole tables.

Watch quality scores in CloudWatch, route results through EventBridge to SNS or Step Functions, and record APIAPI (Application programming interface)A defined way for one program to ask another for data or actions, such as a set of HTTPS requests and responses. Every AWS service is controlled through its API, which the console, the CLI, and the SDKs call for you.Glossary entryClose calls in CloudTrail.
